what_its_for: Pyrimethamine is used to treat and prevent certain parasitic infections. It is most commonly used to treat toxoplasmosis (an infection caused by a parasite called Toxoplasma gondii) and may also be used to prevent or treat malaria. Your doctor may prescribe it along with other medicines, such as a sulfa antibiotic, for the best results.
how_to_take: Take pyrimethamine by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with food or milk if it upsets your stomach. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not stop taking it early without talking to your doctor, even if you feel better. Always take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
dosing: Your dose will depend on your condition, age, weight, and other medicines you are taking. Your doctor will set the right dose for you. Common doses range from 25 mg to 75 mg once daily for adults, but children and people with certain conditions may need different amounts. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store pyrimethamine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from light, heat, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it past the expiration date on the package. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it may increase your risk of side effects. Do not take folic acid supplements (like folate) without talking to your doctor first, as they can make this medicine less effective. However, your doctor may give you a special form of folate called leucovorin (folinic acid) to protect your body. Avoid becoming pregnant while on this medicine unless directed by your doctor, as it may harm an unborn baby. Be careful around people who are sick, as this medicine can weaken your immune system's ability to fight infections.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: unusual bruising or bleeding, extreme tiredness or weakness, pale skin, sore throat or signs of infection (fever, chills), mouth sores, numbness or tingling in your hands or feet, skin rash or blistering, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, or any signs of an allergic reaction such as difficulty breathing, swelling of the face, lips, or tongue. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve or if they get worse.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within a few days of starting treatment, but it is important to finish the full course your doctor prescribed. For toxoplasmosis, treatment usually lasts several weeks. Your doctor will monitor you with blood tests during treatment to make sure the medicine is working and is safe for you.
special_populations: Pregnant women: This medicine can harm a developing baby, especially in the first three months of pregnancy. Tell your doctor immediately if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. Breastfeeding mothers: Pyrimethamine passes into breast milk and may harm a nursing baby. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Dosing in children is based on weight and is carefully calculated by the doctor. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects and may need closer monitoring. Patients with kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor about any kidney or liver conditions, as dose adjustments may be needed.
